question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Not having the ability to read or write.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Illiterate.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Illiterate" means unable to read or write, from Latin illitteratus, formed from in- (not) and litteratus (lettered, educated). (अनपढ़)
◦ Example: The government launched a mission to teach illiterate villagers basic reading and writing skills.

 

• Don't mix up illiterate (a person who cannot read/write) with illegible (writing that cannot be read) or innumerate (a person who cannot do basic maths).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Illegible (अपठनीय / दुर्बोध लिखावट): Writing or print that is not clear enough to be read.

 

• Option 3: Innumerate (अंकों का ज्ञान न रखने वाला): Unable to understand or work with basic numbers.

 

• Option 4: Ignorant (अज्ञानी): Lacking general knowledge or awareness.

 

NOTE

 

• Related education-based words: Literate (able to read and write), Numerate (able to understand numbers), Autodidact (a self-taught person), Erudite (having great knowledge from reading).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Philanthropist (परोपकारी व्यक्ति): A person who generously helps others, especially through charity

2. Misanthrope (मानवद्वेषी): A person who dislikes or distrusts humankind

3. Ambidextrous (दोनों हाथों से समान दक्षता से काम करने वाला): Able to use both hands equally well

4. Gregarious (मिलनसार): Sociable; fond of company

5. Loquacious (बातूनी): Very talkative

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A word that looks the same even when flipped upside down.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Ambigram.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Ambigram" means a word readable even when flipped or rotated, from Latin ambi- (both/around) and Greek gramma (letter), coined for designs readable when rotated or mirrored. (उल्टा-सीधा समान शब्द)
◦ Example: The designer created an ambigram of the couple's names for their wedding invitation.

 

• Don't confuse ambigram (same when visually flipped or rotated) with palindrome (same when read backward as text, e.g. 'MADAM').

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Palindrome (व्यत्यस्त शब्द जो आगे-पीछे दोनों तरफ से एक समान पढ़ा जाए): A word or phrase that reads the same backward as forward.

 

• Option 2: Anagram (अक्षरों को फेरबदल कर बनाया गया शब्द): A word formed by rearranging the letters of another word.

 

• Option 3: Acronym (संक्षिप्ताक्षर): A word formed from the initial letters of a phrase.

 

NOTE

 

• Other wordplay-based one-word substitutions: Palindrome (reads same forward and backward), Anagram (rearranged letters form a new word), Acronym (formed from initial letters), Homograph (same spelling, different meaning).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Sybarite (भोग-विलासी): A person who loves luxury

2. Tacit (मौन / अकथित): Understood or implied without being stated

3. Tangible (मूर्त / स्पर्शनीय): Able to be touched or clearly perceived

4. Taxidermy (पशु संरक्षण कला): The art of preparing and preserving animal skins

5. Ambivalent (दुविधाग्रस्त): Having mixed or contradictory feelings

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Strong public criticism directed at someone.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Censure.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Censure" means strong expression of public disapproval, from Latin censura, from censere (to assess or judge), originally the office of a Roman censor. (निंदा)
◦ Example: The minister faced severe censure from the opposition for his remarks.

 

• Do not confuse censure (to strongly criticize) with censor (to examine and remove or ban objectionable content) — they share a root but differ in meaning.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Eulogy (श्रद्धांजलि / प्रशंसा भाषण): A speech or piece of writing that praises someone highly, especially one who has died.

 

• Option 2: Ovation (हर्षध्वनि / तालियों की गड़गड़ाहट): Enthusiastic applause from an audience.

 

• Option 3: Censorship (सेंसरशिप / निगरानी द्वारा रोक): The suppression or banning of parts of books, films, or news.

 

NOTE

 

• Related criticism/praise words: Eulogy (praise of the dead), Panegyric (formal public praise), Reprimand (an official rebuke), Vilify (to speak evil of someone).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Cynophobia (कुत्तों का भय): An abnormal fear of dogs

2. Claustrophobia (बंद स्थान का भय): An abnormal fear of confined spaces

3. Xenophobia (विदेशियों के प्रति भय या घृणा): Dislike or fear of foreigners or strangers

4. Insomnia (अनिद्रा): Habitual inability to sleep

5. Hypochondriac (रोगभ्रमी): A person excessively anxious about their health

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

An animal that can live both on land and in water.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Amphibian.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Amphibian" means an animal that lives both on land and in water, from Greek amphi- (both) and bios (life). (उभयचर)
◦ Example: The frog is a well-known amphibian that begins life in water as a tadpole.

 

• Remember amphi- means 'both' — an amphibian can live both on land and in water, unlike a reptile which is fully land-adapted.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Reptile (सरीसृप): A cold-blooded, scaly, egg-laying vertebrate such as a snake or lizard.

 

• Option 2: Mammal (स्तनधारी): A warm-blooded vertebrate that feeds its young with milk.

 

• Option 3: Crustacean (कवचधारी जलचर प्राणी): A hard-shelled aquatic invertebrate, such as a crab or lobster.

 

NOTE

 

• Related animal-classification words: Reptile (cold-blooded, scaly land animal), Mammal (warm-blooded, milk-feeding), Invertebrate (animal without a backbone), Herbivore/Carnivore/Omnivore (classified by diet).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Vagabond (आवारा): A person with no fixed home who wanders

2. Nomad (खानाबदोश): A person who moves from place to place, with no fixed residence

3. Mercenary (भाड़े का सैनिक): A professional soldier hired to fight for a foreign army

4. Pediatrician (बाल रोग विशेषज्ञ): A doctor who specializes in children's medical care

5. Cardiologist (हृदय रोग विशेषज्ञ): A doctor who specializes in heart diseases

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Well known for something bad.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Notorious.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Notorious" means well known for something bad, from Latin notorius, from notus (known). (कुख्यात)
◦ Example: The town was notorious for its high crime rate.

 

• Notorious always carries a negative sense, unlike renowned or famous, which are positive; both mean 'widely known' but for opposite reasons.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Renowned (प्रसिद्ध / विख्यात): Famous or well-known for good qualities or achievements.

 

• Option 2: Anonymous (अज्ञात / गुमनाम): Not identified by name; of unknown identity.

 

• Option 4: Prestigious (प्रतिष्ठित): Having a high reputation; respected and admired.

 

NOTE

 

• Contrast with: Renowned (famous for good reasons), Infamous (having a bad reputation, close synonym of notorious), Obscure (not well known), Illustrious (highly distinguished).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Omnivore (सर्वाहारी प्राणी): An animal that eats both plants and animals

2. Nocturnal (रात्रिचर): Active during the night

3. Diurnal (दिनचर): Active during the daytime

4. Autobiography (आत्मकथा): The story of a person's life written by themselves

5. Biography (जीवनी): The story of a person's life written by another

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who believes that pleasure is the most important thing in life.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Epicurean.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Epicurean" means one who believes pleasure is the highest good, named after the Greek philosopher Epicurus, who taught that pleasure was the chief good in life. (भोगवादी)
◦ Example: Being an epicurean, he always sought out the finest food and wine.

 

• Epicurean is the exact opposite of ascetic and stoic, both of which involve denying or enduring rather than seeking pleasure.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Ascetic (तपस्वी / संयमी): A person who practices strict self-denial for religious or spiritual reasons.

 

• Option 2: Stoic (स्थितप्रज्ञ / धैर्यवान): A person who endures pain and hardship without showing feelings.

 

• Option 4: Puritan (कट्टर नैतिकतावादी): A person with strict moral or religious views, opposed to luxury and pleasure.

 

NOTE

 

• Contrast words: Ascetic (practises self-denial), Stoic (indifferent to pleasure and pain), Hedonist (close synonym, pursues pleasure), Puritan (opposed to luxury).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Egoist (अहंकारी / स्वार्थी): A person who is excessively self-centered

2. Zealot (कट्टर समर्थक): A person fanatically devoted to a cause

3. Maverick (स्वतंत्र विचारक): An unorthodox, independent-minded person

4. Novice (नौसिखिया): A person new to and inexperienced in a field

5. Veteran (अनुभवी व्यक्ति): A person with long experience in a particular field

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Clever, original, and inventive.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Ingenious.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Ingenious" means clever, original, and inventive, from Latin ingenium (natural talent, ability); often confused with the unrelated-in-meaning ingenuous (innocent, naive). (कुशाग्र)
◦ Example: She came up with an ingenious solution to the water shortage problem.

 

• Watch the spelling trap: ingenious (clever/inventive) vs ingenuous (innocent/naive) — they look alike but mean very different things.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Ingenuous (भोला-भाला / निष्कपट): Innocent, open, and unsuspecting in character.

 

• Option 3: Disingenuous (कपटपूर्ण / असत्यनिष्ठ): Not candid or sincere, pretending to know less than one does.

 

• Option 4: Genuine (वास्तविक / असली): Truly what it is said to be; authentic.

 

NOTE

 

• Commonly confused pair in SSC: Ingenuous (naive, frank) and Disingenuous (insincere, not straightforward) are opposites of each other, while Ingenious is unrelated in meaning to both.

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Epilogue (उपसंहार): A short concluding section at the end of a literary work

2. Prologue (प्रस्तावना): An introduction at the beginning of a literary work

3. Ornithologist (पक्षी विज्ञानी): A person who studies birds

4. Numismatist (मुद्रा-शास्त्री): A person who studies or collects coins and currency

5. Philatelist (डाक टिकट संग्रहकर्ता): A person who collects postage stamps

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A figure of speech that says less in order to express more.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Litotes.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Litotes" means an understatement using a negative to affirm a positive, from Greek litotes, meaning simplicity or plainness. (अल्पोक्ति)
◦ Example: Saying 'she is not unfamiliar with hardship' is an example of litotes.

 

• Litotes typically uses a negative word to express a positive meaning, e.g. 'not bad' meaning 'good' — the opposite technique of hyperbole, which exaggerates.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Hyperbole (अतिशयोक्ति): A figure of speech using deliberate exaggeration for effect.

 

• Option 2: Euphemism (सौम्योक्ति): A mild or indirect word substituted for a harsh or blunt one.

 

• Option 4: Oxymoron (विरोधाभासी शब्द-युग्म): A figure of speech combining contradictory terms, e.g. 'deafening silence'.

 

NOTE

 

• Related figures of speech: Hyperbole (exaggeration), Euphemism (softened expression), Oxymoron (contradictory terms together), Irony (saying the opposite of what is meant), Metaphor (implied comparison).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Ventriloquist (बिना होंठ हिलाए बोलने वाला कलाकार): A performer who speaks without moving their lips

2. Perjury (झूठी गवाही): The offence of willfully telling a lie under oath

3. Plagiarism (साहित्यिक चोरी): Taking someone else's work and passing it off as one's own

4. Testimony (गवाही / साक्ष्य): A formal written or spoken statement given as evidence

5. Verdict (निर्णय / फैसला): The formal decision or finding of a jury or judge

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A situation with no government or control.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Anarchy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Anarchy" means a state of complete lawlessness with no ruling authority, from Greek anarkhia, from an- (without) and arkhos (ruler). (अराजकता)
◦ Example: The sudden collapse of the government plunged the country into anarchy.

 

• Anarchy means the absence of any government, the opposite of autocracy (rule by one all-powerful person).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Autocracy (निरंकुश शासन / एकतंत्र): A system of government by one person with absolute power.

 

• Option 2: Bureaucracy (नौकरशाही): A system of government administered by officials following fixed rules.

 

• Option 4: Democracy (लोकतंत्र): A system of government by the people, usually through elected representatives.

 

NOTE

 

• Related governance words ending in '-cracy' or '-archy': Autocracy (rule by one), Oligarchy (rule by a small group), Plutocracy (rule by the wealthy), Theocracy (rule by religious authority).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Meteorologist (मौसम वैज्ञानिक): A person who studies and forecasts weather and climate

2. Astronomer (खगोलशास्त्री): A person who studies celestial objects, space, and the universe

3. Archaeologist (पुरातत्वविद्): A person who studies human history through excavation

4. Anthropologist (मानवशास्त्री): A person who studies human societies and cultures

5. Philanthropist (परोपकारी व्यक्ति): A person who generously helps others, especially through charity

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Speaking easily and fluently but without deep thought or sincerity.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Glib.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Glib" means speaking smoothly but without sincerity or real thought, probably from Low German glibberig (slippery), suggesting smooth, slick speech. (सतही)
◦ Example: The salesman gave a glib answer that failed to address our real concerns.

 

• Glib speech sounds fluent but is often shallow or insincere, unlike eloquent speech, which is fluent AND meaningful.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Eloquent (वाक्पटु / सुवक्ता): Fluent and persuasive in speaking or writing.

 

• Option 3: Verbose (शब्दाडंबरपूर्ण / वाचाल): Using more words than necessary; wordy.

 

• Option 4: Reticent (कम बोलने वाला / संकोची): Reserved and not inclined to speak freely.

 

NOTE

 

• Related speech-manner words: Eloquent (fluent, persuasive), Verbose (excessively wordy), Reticent (reserved, saying little), Laconic (using very few words).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Gregarious (मिलनसार): Sociable; fond of company

2. Loquacious (बातूनी): Very talkative

3. Taciturn (मितभाषी): Reserved and saying very little

4. Sycophant (चापलूस): A person who flatters others to gain advantage

5. Sybarite (भोग-विलासी): A person who loves luxury

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who leaves their own country to settle elsewhere.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Emigrant.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Emigrant" means a person who leaves their own country to settle elsewhere, from Latin emigrare, from e- (out of) and migrare (to move). (देश छोड़ने वाला)
◦ Example: Many emigrants left the country in search of better job opportunities abroad.

 

• Remember the direction: an emigrant leaves (exits) a country, while an immigrant enters another country — same journey, viewed from two ends.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Immigrant (आप्रवासी): A person who comes to live permanently in a foreign country.

 

• Option 3: Migrant (प्रवासी): A person who moves from one place to another, often for work.

 

• Option 4: Refugee (शरणार्थी): A person forced to leave their country due to war, persecution, or disaster.

 

NOTE

 

• Related movement-based words: Immigrant (one who enters a new country), Migrant (one who moves, often for work), Refugee (one who flees danger), Expatriate (one living outside their native country).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Taxidermy (पशु संरक्षण कला): The art of preparing and preserving animal skins

2. Ambivalent (दुविधाग्रस्त): Having mixed or contradictory feelings

3. Altruist (परमार्थी): A person who is unselfishly concerned for others' welfare

4. Bibliophile (पुस्तक प्रेमी): A person who loves or collects books

5. Cynophobia (कुत्तों का भय): An abnormal fear of dogs

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A hole dug by an animal for shelter.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Burrow.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Burrow" means a hole dug in the ground for shelter, from Middle English borow/burwe, related to Old English beorgan (to shelter, protect). (बिल)
◦ Example: The rabbit quickly disappeared into its burrow when it sensed danger.

 

• A burrow is specifically a hole dug in the ground, unlike a nest (built above ground, usually by birds) or a lair (a wild predator's resting place, not necessarily dug).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Lair (जंगली पशु की माँद): The resting place or den of a wild animal.

 

• Option 3: Nest (घोंसला): A structure built by a bird or small animal to lay eggs or house its young.

 

• Option 4: Hive (मधुमक्खी का छत्ता): A structure housing a colony of bees.

 

NOTE

 

• Related animal-home words: Nest (bird's home), Lair/Den (wild animal's resting place), Hive (bees' home), Warren (a network of rabbit burrows), Sty (a pig's enclosure).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Insomnia (अनिद्रा): Habitual inability to sleep

2. Hypochondriac (रोगभ्रमी): A person excessively anxious about their health

3. Nostalgia (विगत स्मृति): A sentimental longing for the past

4. Recluse (एकांतवासी): A person who lives in self-imposed isolation

5. Vagabond (आवारा): A person with no fixed home who wanders

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Having very little money.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Impecunious.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Impecunious" means having little or no money, from Latin impecuniosus, from in- (not) and pecunia (money). (निर्धन)
◦ Example: The impecunious writer could barely afford his monthly rent.

 

• Impecunious simply means 'poor', while insolvent specifically means legally unable to pay debts — one can be impecunious without being formally insolvent.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Affluent (धनी / समृद्ध): Having a great deal of money or wealth.

 

• Option 2: Frugal (मितव्ययी / किफायती): Careful and economical in the use of money or resources.

 

• Option 3: Insolvent (दिवालिया): Unable to pay one's debts, especially in a legal sense.

 

NOTE

 

• Related wealth/poverty words: Affluent (wealthy), Frugal (thrifty, careful with money), Destitute (extremely poor, lacking basic necessities), Insolvent (unable to pay debts), Parsimonious (unwilling to spend money).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Pediatrician (बाल रोग विशेषज्ञ): A doctor who specializes in children's medical care

2. Cardiologist (हृदय रोग विशेषज्ञ): A doctor who specializes in heart diseases

3. Herbivore (शाकाहारी प्राणी): An animal that feeds only on plants

4. Carnivore (मांसाहारी प्राणी): An animal that feeds only on flesh

5. Omnivore (सर्वाहारी प्राणी): An animal that eats both plants and animals

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who repairs shoes.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Cobbler.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Cobbler" means a person who mends or makes shoes, origin uncertain, attested in English since the 14th century for a shoe-repairer. (मोची)
◦ Example: The cobbler fixed the torn strap on my old sandals within an hour.

 

• SSC often tests occupation-based one-word substitutions — always link the profession word to the specific material it works with (shoes to cobbler, cloth to tailor, iron to blacksmith).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Tailor (दर्जी): A person who makes, repairs, or alters clothes.

 

• Option 3: Blacksmith (लोहार): A person who makes and repairs things made of iron by hand.

 

• Option 4: Carpenter (बढ़ई): A person who makes and repairs wooden objects and structures.

 

NOTE

 

• Related occupation words: Tailor (clothes), Blacksmith (iron work), Carpenter (woodwork), Potter (clay/pottery), Mason (stone/brick construction).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Autobiography (आत्मकथा): The story of a person's life written by themselves

2. Biography (जीवनी): The story of a person's life written by another

3. Chronology (कालक्रम): The arrangement of events in the order they occurred

4. Ambiguous (अस्पष्ट): Open to more than one interpretation

5. Egoist (अहंकारी / स्वार्थी): A person who is excessively self-centered

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who challenges or attacks established traditions and beliefs.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Iconoclast.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Iconoclast" means one who attacks established beliefs or institutions, from Greek eikon (image) and klastes (breaker), originally referring to destroyers of religious icons. (परंपरा-विरोधी)
◦ Example: As an iconoclast, she was never afraid to question long-held customs of her community.

 

• Iconoclast is the direct opposite of conformist and traditionalist, both of whom accept and follow established norms rather than challenge them.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Conformist (परंपरा-अनुयायी): A person who follows accepted behavior or established customs.

 

• Option 3: Traditionalist (परंपरावादी): A person who upholds and values traditional beliefs or practices.

 

• Option 4: Loyalist (निष्ठावान / वफादार): A person who remains firmly faithful to an established authority or government.

 

NOTE

 

• Contrast words: Conformist (follows norms), Traditionalist (upholds old customs), Loyalist (faithful to authority), Maverick (independent thinker, close in spirit to iconoclast), Rebel (one who resists authority).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Novice (नौसिखिया): A person new to and inexperienced in a field

2. Veteran (अनुभवी व्यक्ति): A person with long experience in a particular field

3. Utopia (काल्पनिक आदर्श स्थान): An imagined place or state in which everything is perfect

4. Anecdote (किस्सा): A short, amusing or interesting story about a real incident

5. Epilogue (उपसंहार): A short concluding section at the end of a literary work

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A group of people who travel with and attend an important person.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Entourage.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Entourage" means attendants who accompany an important person, from French entourer (to surround), from en- and tour (turn, circuit). (साथ चलने वाला समूह)
◦ Example: The film star arrived at the airport surrounded by a large entourage of assistants and bodyguards.

 

• An entourage specifically travels with and attends to one important person, unlike a delegation, which represents a group or organization at an event.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Delegation (प्रतिनिधिमंडल): A group of people sent to represent others, especially at a meeting or conference.

 

• Option 3: Congregation (धार्मिक जनसमूह): A gathering of people, especially for religious worship.

 

• Option 4: Convoy (काफिला): A group of vehicles or ships travelling together, often for protection.

 

NOTE

 

• Related group-of-people words: Delegation (representatives sent to an event), Convoy (vehicles travelling together), Congregation (religious gathering), Retinue (close synonym of entourage, a group of attendants).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Numismatist (मुद्रा-शास्त्री): A person who studies or collects coins and currency

2. Philatelist (डाक टिकट संग्रहकर्ता): A person who collects postage stamps

3. Bibliomania (पुस्तक-उन्माद): An excessive passion for collecting and possessing books

4. Somnambulist (निद्राचारी): A person who walks while asleep

5. Ventriloquist (बिना होंठ हिलाए बोलने वाला कलाकार): A performer who speaks without moving their lips

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

An abnormal fear of flying.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Aerophobia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Aerophobia" means an abnormal fear of flying, from Greek aer (air) and phobos (fear). (उड़ान का भय)
◦ Example: Her aerophobia made even the thought of boarding a plane terrifying.

 

• Don't confuse aerophobia (fear of flying/air) with the similarly spelled acrophobia (fear of heights) — SSC often sets these as a trap pair.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Acrophobia (ऊँचाई का भय): An abnormal fear of heights.

 

• Option 3: Claustrophobia (बंद स्थान का भय): An abnormal fear of confined or enclosed spaces.

 

• Option 4: Hydrophobia (पानी का भय): An abnormal fear of water.

 

NOTE

 

• Other phobia-based one-word substitutions: Acrophobia (heights), Claustrophobia (confined spaces), Hydrophobia (water), Xenophobia (foreigners), Cynophobia (dogs).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Testimony (गवाही / साक्ष्य): A formal written or spoken statement given as evidence

2. Verdict (निर्णय / फैसला): The formal decision or finding of a jury or judge

3. Deforestation (वनोन्मूलन): The large-scale clearing or destruction of forests

4. Ecologist (पारिस्थितिकी विज्ञानी): A person who studies the relationships between organisms and their environment

5. Meteorologist (मौसम वैज्ञानिक): A person who studies and forecasts weather and climate

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Showing aggressive or hostile behavior.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Belligerent.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Belligerent" means aggressively hostile and ready to fight, from Latin belligerare (to wage war), from bellum (war) and gerere (to carry on). (लड़ाकू)
◦ Example: The belligerent customer shouted at the staff over a minor billing error.

 

• Belligerent is the opposite of amiable and docile — it describes a person eager for conflict, not one who is calm or cooperative.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Amiable (मिलनसार / मृदुभाषी): Friendly and pleasant in manner.

 

• Option 2: Docile (विनम्र / आज्ञाकारी): Easy to manage or teach; submissive.

 

• Option 3: Diplomatic (कूटनीतिक): Skilled in handling sensitive matters tactfully without causing offence.

 

NOTE

 

• Related war/aggression words: Bellicose (close synonym, warlike in nature), Hostile (unfriendly, antagonistic), Truculent (fierce and quick to argue), Pugnacious (eager to fight or argue).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Anthropologist (मानवशास्त्री): A person who studies human societies and cultures

2. Philanthropist (परोपकारी व्यक्ति): A person who generously helps others, especially through charity

3. Misanthrope (मानवद्वेषी): A person who dislikes or distrusts humankind

4. Ambidextrous (दोनों हाथों से समान दक्षता से काम करने वाला): Able to use both hands equally well

5. Gregarious (मिलनसार): Sociable; fond of company

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Made up of different kinds or elements.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Heterogeneous.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Heterogeneous" means consisting of diverse or dissimilar elements, from Greek heteros (other/different) and genos (kind). (विजातीय)
◦ Example: India has a heterogeneous population made up of many languages, religions, and cultures.

 

• Remember the Greek roots: hetero- means 'different' and homo- means 'same' — so heterogeneous and homogeneous are direct opposites.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Homogeneous (सजातीय / एकरूप): Consisting of parts that are all the same kind.

 

• Option 3: Uniform (एकसमान): Not varying; the same in all parts or cases.

 

• Option 4: Composite (मिश्रित / संयुक्त): Made up of various parts or materials combined together.

 

NOTE

 

• Common hetero-/homo- opposite pairs tested in SSC: Heterogeneous vs Homogeneous, Heterosexual vs Homosexual, Heterodox (unorthodox) vs Orthodox (conventional).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Sycophant (चापलूस): A person who flatters others to gain advantage

2. Sybarite (भोग-विलासी): A person who loves luxury

3. Tacit (मौन / अकथित): Understood or implied without being stated

4. Tangible (मूर्त / स्पर्शनीय): Able to be touched or clearly perceived

5. Taxidermy (पशु संरक्षण कला): The art of preparing and preserving animal skins

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Impossible to defeat or enter by force.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Impregnable.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Impregnable" means too strong to be defeated or entered by force, from Latin in- (not) and prehendere (to seize), literally 'not able to be seized'. (अभेद्य)
◦ Example: The ancient fort was considered impregnable due to its massive stone walls.

 

• Impregnable is the exact opposite of vulnerable — it describes something so strong or well-defended that it cannot be captured or broken into.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Vulnerable (असुरक्षित / भेद्य): Exposed to being easily attacked, harmed, or defeated.

 

• Option 2: Fragile (नाजुक / भंगुर): Easily broken, damaged, or destroyed.

 

• Option 3: Susceptible (प्रभावित होने योग्य): Likely to be influenced or harmed by a particular thing.

 

NOTE

 

• Related strength/security words: Invincible (cannot be defeated), Invulnerable (cannot be harmed), Unassailable (cannot be attacked or questioned), Fortified (strengthened for defence).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Bibliophile (पुस्तक प्रेमी): A person who loves or collects books

2. Cynophobia (कुत्तों का भय): An abnormal fear of dogs

3. Claustrophobia (बंद स्थान का भय): An abnormal fear of confined spaces

4. Xenophobia (विदेशियों के प्रति भय या घृणा): Dislike or fear of foreigners or strangers

5. Insomnia (अनिद्रा): Habitual inability to sleep

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who studies the origin and history of words.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Etymologist.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Etymologist" means a specialist in the origin and history of words, from Greek etymon (true sense/origin) and logos (study). (व्युत्पत्तिवेत्ता)
◦ Example: The etymologist explained that the word 'salary' comes from the Latin word for salt.

 

• An etymologist focuses specifically on the origin and history of individual words, while a lexicographer compiles those words into a dictionary.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Linguist (भाषाविद्): A person who studies languages or is skilled in several languages.

 

• Option 2: Lexicographer (शब्दकोशकार): A person who compiles or writes dictionaries.

 

• Option 4: Philologist (भाषाशास्त्री): A person who studies the historical development and structure of languages.

 

NOTE

 

• Related language-study words ending in '-ist'/'-ian': Linguist (studies languages), Philologist (studies language history/structure), Lexicographer (compiles dictionaries), Grammarian (studies grammar rules).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Recluse (एकांतवासी): A person who lives in self-imposed isolation

2. Vagabond (आवारा): A person with no fixed home who wanders

3. Nomad (खानाबदोश): A person who moves from place to place, with no fixed residence

4. Mercenary (भाड़े का सैनिक): A professional soldier hired to fight for a foreign army

5. Pediatrician (बाल रोग विशेषज्ञ): A doctor who specializes in children's medical care

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Extending across or applying to different historical periods.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Transhistorical.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Transhistorical" means existing across or beyond all historical periods, from Latin trans- (across/beyond) combined with historical, denoting something that holds true across all eras. (कालातीत)
◦ Example: Some scholars argue that human curiosity is a transhistorical trait found in every era.

 

• Transhistorical means something applies across all time periods, unlike contemporary, which is limited to the present time only.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Contemporary (समकालीन): Belonging to or occurring in the present time.

 

• Option 3: Chronological (कालानुक्रमिक): Arranged in the order in which events occurred.

 

• Option 4: Anachronistic (कालविपर्यय संबंधी): Belonging to a period other than the one being depicted or described.

 

NOTE

 

• Related time-based words: Contemporary (present-day), Chronological (in time order), Anachronistic (out of its proper time period), Timeless (close synonym, unaffected by passage of time).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Carnivore (मांसाहारी प्राणी): An animal that feeds only on flesh

2. Omnivore (सर्वाहारी प्राणी): An animal that eats both plants and animals

3. Nocturnal (रात्रिचर): Active during the night

4. Diurnal (दिनचर): Active during the daytime

5. Autobiography (आत्मकथा): The story of a person's life written by themselves

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Very unwilling to spend money.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Parsimonious.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Parsimonious" means extremely reluctant to spend money, from Latin parsimonia (thrift), from parcere (to spare). (कंजूस)
◦ Example: The parsimonious old man refused to buy new clothes even though he could afford them.

 

• Parsimonious is the opposite of both generous and extravagant/prodigal — it describes excessive unwillingness to spend, close to miserly.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Generous (उदार / दानशील): Willing to give freely and share with others.

 

• Option 2: Extravagant (फिजूलखर्च): Spending money excessively or lavishly.

 

• Option 4: Prodigal (उड़ाऊ / अपव्ययी): Wastefully or recklessly extravagant with money or resources.

 

NOTE

 

• Related money-attitude words: Miserly (close synonym, extremely stingy), Frugal (careful but not necessarily stingy), Extravagant/Prodigal (spending wastefully), Generous (giving freely).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Ambiguous (अस्पष्ट): Open to more than one interpretation

2. Egoist (अहंकारी / स्वार्थी): A person who is excessively self-centered

3. Zealot (कट्टर समर्थक): A person fanatically devoted to a cause

4. Maverick (स्वतंत्र विचारक): An unorthodox, independent-minded person

5. Novice (नौसिखिया): A person new to and inexperienced in a field

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A feeling of great excitement or happiness.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Exhilaration.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Exhilaration" means a feeling of great excitement and happiness, from Latin exhilarare (to gladden), from ex- (thoroughly) and hilarare (to cheer, related to hilarus, cheerful). (आनंद)
◦ Example: She felt a rush of exhilaration as the roller coaster plunged down the first drop.

 

• Exhilaration is a positive, energizing emotion — the opposite of melancholy (sadness) or apathy (indifference).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Melancholy (उदासी / विषाद): A deep, pensive, and long-lasting sadness.

 

• Option 3: Apathy (उदासीनता): A lack of interest, enthusiasm, or concern.

 

• Option 4: Trepidation (भय / आशंका): A feeling of fear or anxiety about something that may happen.

 

NOTE

 

• Related emotion words: Melancholy (sadness), Apathy (indifference), Trepidation (anxious fear), Euphoria (close synonym, intense happiness), Ecstasy (overwhelming joy).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Anecdote (किस्सा): A short, amusing or interesting story about a real incident

2. Epilogue (उपसंहार): A short concluding section at the end of a literary work

3. Prologue (प्रस्तावना): An introduction at the beginning of a literary work

4. Ornithologist (पक्षी विज्ञानी): A person who studies birds

5. Numismatist (मुद्रा-शास्त्री): A person who studies or collects coins and currency

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

An agent or cause of someone's downfall or deserved punishment.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Nemesis.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Nemesis" means an agent of retribution or inevitable downfall, from Nemesis, the Greek goddess of divine retribution and vengeance. (दंड)
◦ Example: Overconfidence proved to be the champion's nemesis in the final match.

 

• In modern usage, nemesis can also refer to a long-standing rival, but its core sense is an unavoidable cause of someone's ruin or just punishment, unlike an ally, who supports rather than defeats.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Ally (सहयोगी / मित्र): A person or group that cooperates with another for a common purpose.

 

• Option 3: Benefactor (दानदाता / उपकारकर्ता): A person who gives financial or other help to a person or cause.

 

• Option 4: Advocate (पक्षसमर्थक): A person who publicly supports or argues in favour of a cause or person.

 

NOTE

 

• Mythology-derived one-word substitutions: Nemesis (Greek goddess of retribution), Herculean (a task requiring great strength, from Hercules), Utopia (an ideal imaginary place), Chimera (an illusory or impossible idea, from the mythical creature).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Somnambulist (निद्राचारी): A person who walks while asleep

2. Ventriloquist (बिना होंठ हिलाए बोलने वाला कलाकार): A performer who speaks without moving their lips

3. Perjury (झूठी गवाही): The offence of willfully telling a lie under oath

4. Plagiarism (साहित्यिक चोरी): Taking someone else's work and passing it off as one's own

5. Testimony (गवाही / साक्ष्य): A formal written or spoken statement given as evidence
